version: LOCK 3 V1 (7 Nov 2026) - chapter 1: the open purse, hadith page 1, the bread grab, What people say
builds_on: LOCK 1 V2 (foundations.json) and LOCK 2 V3 (identity.json). Placeholders: {n} number, {teacher} teacher name, {word} learned-word display, {ar}/{en} word parts.

places.inn: People are waiting at the door

purse.title: People at the inn door
purse.intro: Word has spread: a foreigner with a heavy purse is at the inn. Nadir, the innkeeper’s son, knows a little of your language and explains for them.
purse.only_public: You can only give where people can see, for now.
purse.ask_baker: Ask Salma the baker about them

people.name: Yusuf, a father with a sick son
people.ask: His son Ali has a fever. Rania the healer wants ten coins.

people.name: Faris, a boy with bare feet
people.ask: The orphan from the quay points at your shoes, then at his feet. Three coins buys a pair.

people.name: Tariq, who says he lost everything
people.ask: He says his house burned down last week, and asks for twenty coins.

people.name: Umm Salim, a widow
people.ask: She would never ask. Salma says she has hardly eaten in days. Eight coins feeds her for a month.

baker.title: Salma the baker
lines: Salma knows everyone on the street. She nods at Yusuf and at Faris. About Tariq and his burned house she only shrugs.
Then she says quietly: Umm Salim, the widow at the end of the lane, has hardly eaten in days. She would never come and ask.
She wraps your bread in an old page covered in writing you cannot read.

morning.kicker: Chapter 1 · The open purse · next morning
morning.title: What the street saw
morning.crowd: By morning word has spread. {n} people are waiting at the inn door.
morning.quiet: The inn door is quiet this morning.
morning.none: Nobody is waiting any more. People say the foreigner keeps his purse shut.
morning.father_public: Yusuf walks past with Ali, who is on his feet again. He tells the whole street who paid.
morning.father_secret: Yusuf tells everyone Rania was paid by someone he never saw. He does not know it was you.
morning.boy: Faris runs past the quay in new shoes.
morning.fire: Salma shakes her head: Tariq’s house never burned. He tries it on every new traveller - and now he is telling everyone how easy you were.
morning.widow_secret: Warm bread has been left at your door. You never find out who left it.
morning.widow_public: Umm Salim keeps her eyes down when she sees you. Half the street watched her take your coins.

page.title: A page wrapped round bread
page.story: {teacher} holds the page up to the light and goes quiet. He knows the hand: the scholar people still tell stories about, who travelled the land collecting the sayings of the Prophet, peace be upon him. They say he paid a whole street’s debts at night, and nobody knew until he died.
page.hadith: {teacher} reads it with you, word by word. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said seven people will be shaded by Allah on the day there is no shade but His - among them, one who gives in charity {word}, so secretly that the left hand does not know what the right hand has given.
page.learned: New word: {ar} = {en} · New: you can give in secret

see.title: At the oven
see.text: Mid-morning in the square. Faris, the orphan boy from the quay, slips a loaf off Salma’s tray and runs. Salma is turned away. Nobody else is close.

ask.title: Salma stops you
ask.text: That afternoon Salma stops you, flour on her hands. Nadir translates: “You were in the square this morning. Did you see who took my bread?”

truth.button: Tell the truth: it was Faris
truth.out: Salma thanks you and chases Faris away from her oven. Faris will not look at you now.

lie.out: Faris tells the other quay boys the foreigner covered for him. By evening Salma has heard. “You looked me in the eye,” she says.

quiet.out: Salma sighs and goes back to her oven.

pay.button: Pay for the loaf yourself (1 coin)
pay.out: Salma takes the coin, puzzled. A few days later Faris starts carrying wood for her oven - someone told him who paid.
say: Paid for a hungry boy’s bread

after.title: What came of it
after.note: A lie only gets out through people - here, because Faris talks.

rep.title: River Market · trust {n} / 100
rep.empty: Nobody in River Market talks about you yet. To them you are just “the foreigner”.
rep.secret_note: Gifts nobody saw are not here. Only you know about them.
rep.towns_note: The towns beyond the gates have not heard of you yet.
rep.task_amended: Cut a corner, then put it right
widow_public: Gave to Umm Salim in front of everyone
